scenarios.scenario-1: The IR is deterministic: two builds from the same graph produce identical text and graph sha256; components are sorted modules, boundaries are TYPE groups, and cards report declared vs depicted dependencies and verification coverage.
scenarios.scenario-2: `--format json` returns the IR plus the full dependency list; `--format mermaid` renders every declared edge; both work with Archify absent (exit 0).
scenarios.scenario-3: `--format html` with a fake Archify CLI runs validate then deliver, writes IR + HTML + receipt (declared vs depicted counts, validation=passed) and exits 0; the .mjs entry runs through the Node runner when node is available.
scenarios.scenario-4: Missing Archify on format=html, schema rejection, delivery failure and non-JSON output all exit 1 with the documented code/text; a rejected IR writes no IR/HTML, a delivery failure keeps the refreshed IR. `<out>` outside the root, non-HTML out, invalid format and unsupported kind exit 2.
scenarios.scenario-5: `--check` exits 1 with DIAGRAM_STALE for a missing or tampered committed IR and exits 0 when the IR matches the current graph.

required-log-markers.marker-1: No runtime log markers; behavior is asserted through CLI text/exit codes, artifacts and receipts.

notes.note-1: Covered by test/grace-diagram.test.ts (13 tests: deterministic IR, mapping, backbone, Mermaid, fake-Archify validate/deliver, degradation, --check, usage errors).
notes.note-2: Real-binary evidence (manual): `mygrace diagram --format html` validated and delivered against Archify 3.2.0 and 3.3.x CLIs; `--check` passed on the committed IR.
notes.note-3: No Archify installed → JSON/Mermaid unaffected; only explicit format=html reports INTEGRATION_UNAVAILABLE (exit 1).
